title: The special clarinet chorus on St. Louis Blues
summary: Barnes says the clarinet chorus did not come from the orchestra; the band simply liked it and left it for the clarinet.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Sidney Bechet: the man, the horn, the legend

blocks.x: Well, I want to ask you about another tune that there's a special clarinet part now that a lot of the old timers play at the St. Louis Blues. Oh, well yeah, that's a special. That's a special.

Yeah, St. Louis Blues, that's a special clarinet in there. But that doesn't come from the orchestra. No. No, it didn't come from the orchestra, because we played it, we just liked it, that part in it, so the band would leave a clarinet mate there. So that's a special chorus, isn't it? Yeah, a special chorus. Whose chorus is it? No, I mean, is there any clarinet player that taught it up, any one guy? Where did you first hear it?
Well, I don't know, over the way I got it at, but I'll tell you the truth.

Years ago, a long time ago, we couldn't play nothing but that for the boys. Like we had our boy here at Simon J. Peterson's school up there, and we know the band could play by the table at school. You see, on a certain reason, just on that part, they thought it was so fine, they gritted, and men of them were liking it.
